physical_harm: Two persons died due to lathi blows
motive: Grudge over a money settlement agreement
key_evidence_accepted: The court accepted the claim of the appellants that they were defending themselves against an attack, hence had a right of private defence insofar as the death of 'R' was concerned. However, they were not justified in chasing 'P' and causing fatal injuries on him as the reasonable apprehension had disappeared when 'P' started running away.
witness_credibility: The court found the evidence of PW-7, PW-8, and PW-10 (injured eye-witnesses and son of 'P') to be credible and corroborative, supporting the prosecution's case that the appellants chased 'P' and inflicted fatal injuries on him.
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that a fight between two rival groups resulted in the deaths of 'R' and 'P' due to lathi blows inflicted by the appellants. They relied on the evidence of injured eye-witnesses (PW-7 and PW-8) and the son of 'P' (PW-10) to support their case.
defence_argument: The appellants argued that they were defending themselves against an attack by the complainant's party, who had initiated the aggression. They claimed they had a right to private defence and were therefore entitled to acquittal.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the burden of proof lies on the accused to establish the plea of self-defence, and that the defence must be a reasonable and probable version satisfying the court that the harm caused was necessary to ward off the attack or prevent further apprehension.
precedent_relied_upon: V. Subramani & Anr. v. State of T.N. (2005) 10 SCC 358
sentencing_rationale: The court found that the appellants exceeded their right of private defence by chasing 'P' and causing fatal injuries, thus justifying the conviction under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the IPC and the life sentence awarded.
